title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, The Law Established Through Faith, Discourse Two. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.

title: We establish the law
english: Do we then make the law void through faith? God forbid! Yes, we establish the law. Romans 3:31.

title: Making the law void
english: It has been shown in the preceding discourse what the most usual ways are of making the law void through faith: first, not preaching it at all, which effectively makes it all void at a stroke — and this under color of preaching Christ and magnifying the gospel, though in truth it destroys both the one and the other. Second, teaching (whether directly or indirectly) that faith supersedes the necessity of holiness: that holiness is less necessary now, or a lesser degree of it necessary, than before Christ came; that it is less necessary to us because we believe than it would otherwise have been; or that Christian liberty is a liberty from any kind or degree of holiness — so perverting those great truths that we are now under the covenant of grace and not of works, that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law (Romans 3:28), and that to him who does not work but believes, his faith is counted for righteousness (Romans 4:5). Or third, doing this practically: making the law void in practice though not in principle, living or acting as if faith were designed to excuse us from holiness, allowing ourselves in sin because we are not under the law but under grace (Romans 6:14). It remains to inquire how we may follow a better pattern, how we may be able to say with the apostle, Do we then make the law void through faith? God forbid! Yes, we establish the law (Romans 3:31).

title: The moral law
english: We do not indeed establish the old ceremonial law; we know that is abolished forever. Much less do we establish the whole Mosaic dispensation. This, we know, our Lord has nailed to his cross (Colossians 2:14). Nor yet do we so establish the moral law (which, it is to be feared, too many do) as if fulfilling it, keeping all the commandments, were the condition of our justification. If it were so, surely in his sight no living man would be justified (Psalm 143:2). But with all this allowed, we still, in the apostle's sense, establish the law, the moral law.

title: By our doctrine
english: We establish the law, first, by our doctrine: by endeavoring to preach it in its whole extent, to explain and enforce every part of it in the same manner as our great Teacher did while on earth. We establish it by following Saint Peter's advice: If any man speaks, let him speak as the oracles of God (1 Peter 4:11); as the holy men of old, moved by the Holy Spirit, spoke and wrote for our instruction (2 Peter 1:21), and as the apostles of our blessed Lord did by the direction of the same Spirit. We establish it whenever we speak in his name by keeping back nothing from those who hear, by declaring to them without any limitation or reserve the whole counsel of God (Acts 20:27). And in order to establish it more effectively, we use great plainness of speech. We are not like many who corrupt the word of God, who adulterate it as dishonest sellers do their bad wine; we do not water it down, mix, adulterate, or soften it to suit the taste of the hearers. But as of sincerity, as of God, in the sight of God we speak in Christ (2 Corinthians 2:17), having no other aim than by manifestation of the truth to commend ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God (2 Corinthians 4:2).

title: The whole law
english: We then by our doctrine establish the law when we thus openly declare it to all men, and that in the fullness in which it is delivered by our blessed Lord and his apostles: when we publish it in its height and depth and length and breadth (Ephesians 3:18). We then establish the law when we declare every part of it, every commandment contained in it, not only in its full literal sense but likewise in its spiritual meaning: not only with regard to the outward actions which it either forbids or enjoins, but also with respect to the inward principle, to the thoughts, desires, and intents of the heart.

title: A hidden mystery
english: And indeed we do this the more diligently, not only because it is of the deepest importance — inasmuch as all the fruit, every word and work, must be only evil continually if the tree is evil, if the dispositions and tempers of the heart are not right before God — but likewise because, as important as these things are, they are little considered or understood. So little that we may truly say of the law too, when taken in its full spiritual meaning, that it is a mystery hidden from ages and generations since the world began (Colossians 1:26). It was utterly hidden from the heathen world. They, with all their boasted wisdom, neither found out God nor the law of God, neither in the letter nor much less in the spirit of it. Their foolish hearts were more and more darkened, and while professing themselves wise they became fools (Romans 1:22). And it was almost equally hidden, as to its spiritual meaning, from the bulk of the Jewish nation. Even those who were so ready to declare concerning others, This people who do not know the law are accursed (John 7:49), pronounced their own sentence in it, being under the same curse of the same dreadful ignorance. Witness our Lord's continual reproof of the wisest among them for their gross misinterpretations of it. Witness the supposition almost universally received among them, that they needed only to make clean the outside of the cup (Matthew 23:25); that paying tithe of mint, anise, and cumin, that outward exactness, would atone for inward unholiness, for the total neglect both of justice and mercy, of faith and the love of God (Matthew 23:23). Yes, so absolutely was the spiritual meaning of the law hidden from the wisest of them that one of their most eminent rabbis comments thus on those words of the psalmist, If I incline to iniquity with my heart, the Lord will not hear me (Psalm 66:18): that is, he says, if it is only in my heart, if I do not commit outward wickedness, the Lord will not regard it; he will not punish me unless I proceed to the outward act!

title: Strangers to the law
english: But alas, the law of God, as to its inward spiritual meaning, is hidden not from Jews or heathens only, but even from what is called the Christian world — at least from a vast majority of them. The spiritual sense of the commandments of God is still a mystery to them also. Nor is this observable only in those lands which are overspread with Romish darkness and ignorance. But this is too sure: the far greater part even of those who are called reformed Christians are utter strangers to this day to the law of Christ in its purity and spirituality.

title: Speak the truth
english: Hence it is that to this day the scribes and Pharisees, the men who have the form but not the power of religion, and who are generally wise in their own eyes and righteous in their own conceits, hearing these things are offended — deeply offended when we speak of the religion of the heart, and particularly when we show that without this, even if we gave all our goods to feed the poor, it would profit us nothing (1 Corinthians 13:3). But offended they must be, for we cannot but speak the truth as it is in Jesus. It is our part, whether they will hear or whether they will refuse to hear (Ezekiel 2:7), to deliver our own soul (Ezekiel 3:19). All that is written in the book of God we are to declare, not as pleasing men but God (1 Thessalonians 2:4). We are to declare not only all the promises but all the threatenings too which we find in it. At the same time as we proclaim all the blessings and privileges which God has prepared for his children, we are likewise to teach all the things whatsoever he has commanded (Matthew 28:20). And we know that all these have their use: either for awakening those who sleep (Ephesians 5:14), instructing the ignorant, comforting the feeble-minded (1 Thessalonians 5:14), or building up and perfecting the saints. We know that all Scripture given by inspiration of God is profitable either for doctrine or for reproof, either for correction or for instruction in righteousness, and that the man of God, in the process of the work of God in his soul, has need of every part of it, so that he may at length be perfect, thoroughly furnished to all good works (2 Timothy 3:16-17).

title: Christ in all his offices
english: It is our part thus to preach Christ by preaching all things whatsoever he has revealed. We may indeed without blame — yes, and with a peculiar blessing from God — declare the love of our Lord Jesus Christ. We may speak in a more special manner of the Lord our righteousness (Jeremiah 23:6). We may expatiate upon the grace of God in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Corinthians 5:19). We may at proper opportunities dwell upon his praise as bearing the iniquities of us all, as wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our iniquities, so that by his stripes we might be healed (Isaiah 53:5). But still we would not preach Christ according to his word if we were wholly to confine ourselves to this. We are not ourselves clear before God unless we proclaim him in all his offices. To preach Christ as a workman who needs not to be ashamed (2 Timothy 2:15) is to preach him not only as our great high priest, taken from among men and ordained for men in things pertaining to God (Hebrews 5:1), as such reconciling us to God by his blood and ever living to make intercession for us (Hebrews 7:25), but likewise as the prophet of the Lord who of God is made to us wisdom (1 Corinthians 1:30); who by his word and his Spirit is with us always (Matthew 28:20), guiding us into all truth (John 16:13); yes, and as remaining a King forever, as giving laws to all whom he has bought with his blood, as restoring those to the image of God whom he had first reinstated in his favor, as reigning in all believing hearts until he has subdued all things to himself (Philippians 3:21), until he has utterly cast out all sin and brought in everlasting righteousness (Daniel 9:24).

title: Faith produces holiness
english: We establish the law, second, when we so preach faith in Christ as not to supersede but to produce holiness: to produce every kind of holiness, negative and positive, of the heart and of the life.

title: The handmaid of love
english: In order to this, we continually declare (what should be frequently and deeply considered by all who would not make the law void through faith) that faith itself, even Christian faith, the faith of God's elect, the faith of the operation of God (Colossians 2:12), still is only the handmaid of love. As glorious and honorable as it is, it is not the end of the commandment. God has given this honor to love alone: love is the end of all the commandments of God (1 Timothy 1:5). Love is the end, the sole end, of every dispensation of God from the beginning of the world to the consummation of all things. And it will endure when heaven and earth flee away, for love alone never fails (1 Corinthians 13:8). Faith will totally fail; it will be swallowed up in sight, in the everlasting vision of God. But even then love —

title: Deathless triumph
english: Its nature and its office still the same, lasting its lamp and unconsumed its flame, in deathless triumph shall forever live, and endless good diffuse and endless praise receive.

title: Love excels faith
english: Very excellent things are spoken of faith, and whoever partakes of it may well say with the apostle, Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift (2 Corinthians 9:15). Yet still it loses all its excellence when brought into comparison with love. What Saint Paul observes concerning the superior glory of the gospel above that of the law may with great propriety be spoken of the superior glory of love above that of faith: even that which was made glorious has no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excels (2 Corinthians 3:10). For if that which is done away is glorious, much more does that which remains exceed in glory (2 Corinthians 3:11). Yes, all the glory of faith before it is done away arises from this: that it ministers to love. It is the great temporary means which God has ordained to promote that eternal end.

title: Before faith was
english: Let those who magnify faith beyond all proportion so as to swallow up all else, and who so totally misapprehend its nature as to imagine it stands in the place of love, consider further that as love will exist after faith, so it existed long before it. The angels, who from the moment of their creation beheld the face of their Father who is in heaven (Matthew 18:10), had no occasion for faith in its general notion, as the evidence of things not seen (Hebrews 11:1). Nor did they need faith in its more particular acceptation, faith in the blood of Jesus, for he did not take on himself the nature of angels, but only the seed of Abraham (Hebrews 2:16). There was therefore no place before the foundation of the world for faith either in the general or the particular sense. But there was a place for love. Love existed from eternity in God, the great ocean of love. Love had a place in all the children of God from the moment of their creation. They received at once from their gracious Creator existence and love.

title: Adam walked by sight
english: Nor is it certain (as ingeniously and plausibly as many have discoursed on this) that faith, even in the general sense of the word, had any place in paradise. It is highly probable, from the brief and sparing account which we have in holy writ, that Adam before he rebelled against God walked with him by sight and not by faith (2 Corinthians 5:7).

title: Reason's eye
english: For then his reason's eye was strong and clear, and as an eagle can behold the sun, he might have beheld his Maker's face as near as the intellectual angels could have done.

title: Face to face
english: He was then able to talk with him face to face whose face we cannot now see and live (Exodus 33:20), and consequently had no need of that faith whose office it is to supply the lack of sight.

title: Faith was added
english: On the other hand, it is absolutely certain that faith in its particular sense had then no place. For in that sense it necessarily presupposes sin and the wrath of God declared against the sinner, without which there is no need of an atonement for sin in order to the sinner's reconciliation with God. Consequently, as there was no need of an atonement before the fall, so there was no place for faith in that atonement, man being then pure from every stain of sin, holy as God is holy (1 Peter 1:15-16). But love even then filled his heart. It reigned in him without a rival. And it was only when love was lost by sin that faith was added, not for its own sake nor with any design that it should exist any longer than until it had answered the end for which it was ordained — namely, to restore man to the love from which he had fallen. At the fall therefore was added this evidence of things unseen (Hebrews 11:1), which before was utterly needless: this confidence in redeeming love, which could not possibly have any place until the promise was made that the seed of the woman would bruise the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15).

title: Designed to restore love
english: Faith then was originally designed by God to reestablish the law of love. Therefore in speaking thus we are not undervaluing it or robbing it of its due praise; on the contrary, we are showing its real worth, exalting it in its just proportion, and giving it the very place which the wisdom of God assigned it from the beginning. It is the grand means of restoring that holy love in which man was originally created. It follows that although faith is of no value in itself (as neither is any other means whatsoever), yet as it leads to that end — the establishing anew of the law of love in our hearts — and as in the present state of things it is the only means under heaven for effecting it, it is on that account an unspeakable blessing to man and of unspeakable value before God.

title: In our own hearts
english: And this naturally brings us to observe, third, the most important way of establishing the law: namely, establishing it in our own hearts and lives. Indeed without this, what would all the rest avail? We might establish it by our doctrine; we might preach it in its whole extent, and explain and enforce every part of it. We might open it in its most spiritual meaning and declare the mysteries of the kingdom; we might preach Christ in all his offices, and faith in Christ as opening all the treasures of his love. And yet all this time, if the law we preached were not established in our hearts, we would be of no more account before God than sounding brass or tinkling cymbals (1 Corinthians 13:1). All our preaching, so far from profiting ourselves, would only increase our damnation.

title: Only by faith
english: This is therefore the main point to be considered: how may we establish the law in our own hearts so that it may have its full influence on our lives? And this can only be done by faith.

title: Walk by faith
english: Faith alone it is which effectively answers this end, as we learn from daily experience. For so long as we walk by faith and not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7), we go swiftly on in the way of holiness. While we steadily look not at the things which are seen but at those which are not seen (2 Corinthians 4:18), we are more and more crucified to the world and the world crucified to us (Galatians 6:14). Let but the eye of the soul be constantly fixed, not on the things which are temporal but on those which are eternal, and our affections are more and more loosened from earth and fixed on things above (Colossians 3:2). So that faith in general is the most direct and effective means of promoting all righteousness and true holiness: of establishing the holy and spiritual law in the hearts of those who believe.

title: Love fulfills the law
english: And by faith, taken in its more particular meaning, as confidence in a pardoning God, we establish his law in our own hearts in a still more effective manner. For there is no motive which so powerfully inclines us to love God as the sense of the love of God in Christ. Nothing enables us like a piercing conviction of this to give our hearts to him who was given for us. And from this principle of grateful love to God arises love to our brother also. Nor can we avoid loving our neighbor if we truly believe the love with which God has loved us (1 John 4:16). Now this love for man, grounded on faith and love toward God, works no ill to our neighbor. Consequently it is (as the apostle observes) the fulfilling of the whole negative law: for this — You shall not commit adultery, You shall not kill, You shall not steal, You shall not bear false witness, You shall not covet (Exodus 20:13-17) — and if there is any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying: You shall love your neighbor as yourself (Romans 13:9). Nor is love content with merely working no evil to our neighbor. It continually incites us to do good, as we have time and opportunity, to do good in every possible kind and in every possible degree to all men (Galatians 6:10). It is therefore the fulfilling of the positive likewise, as well as of the negative law of God.

title: Purifying the heart
english: Nor does faith fulfill either the negative or the positive law as to the external part only; but it works inwardly by love (Galatians 5:6) to the purifying of the heart, cleansing it from all vile affections. Everyone who has this faith in him purifies himself even as he is pure (1 John 3:3): purifies himself from every earthly, sensual desire, from all vile and inordinate affections — yes, from the whole of that carnal mind which is enmity against God (Romans 8:7). At the same time, if it has its perfect work, it fills him with all goodness, righteousness, and truth (Ephesians 5:9). It brings all heaven into his soul and causes him to walk in the light even as God is in the light (1 John 1:7).

title: Hold fast
english: Let us thus endeavor to establish the law in ourselves: not sinning because we are under grace (Romans 6:15), but rather using all the power we receive by grace to fulfill all righteousness. Calling to mind what light we received from God while his Spirit was convincing us of sin, let us beware that we do not put out that light; what we had then attained, let us hold fast (Revelation 3:3). Let nothing induce us to build again what we have destroyed (Galatians 2:18): to resume anything, small or great, which we then clearly saw was not for the glory of God or the profit of our own soul, or to neglect anything, small or great, which we could not then neglect without a check from our own conscience. To increase and perfect the light which we had before, let us now add the light of faith. Let us confirm the former gift of God by a deeper sense of whatever he had then shown us, by a greater tenderness of conscience and a more exquisite sensibility of sin. Walking now with joy and not with fear, in a clear, steady sight of things eternal, we shall look on pleasure, wealth, praise, all the things of earth, as on bubbles upon the water, counting nothing important, nothing desirable, nothing worth a deliberate thought, but only what is within the veil, where Jesus sits at the right hand of God (Colossians 3:1).

title: From faith to faith
english: Can you say, You are merciful to my unrighteousness; my sins you remember no more (Hebrews 8:12)? Then for the time to come, see that you flee from sin as from the face of a serpent (Sirach 21:2). For how exceedingly sinful does it appear to you now? How heinous beyond all expression? On the other hand, in how lovely a light do you now see the holy and perfect will of God? Now therefore labor so that it may be fulfilled both in you, by you, and upon you. Now watch and pray (Matthew 26:41) that you may sin no more, that you may see and shun the least transgression of his law. You see the motes which you could not see before, when the sun shines into a dark place. In the same manner, you see the sins which you could not see before, now that the Sun of Righteousness shines in your heart (Malachi 4:2). Now then be diligent in every respect to walk according to the light you have received. Now be zealous to receive more light daily: more of the knowledge and love of God, more of the Spirit of Christ, more of his life and of the power of his resurrection (Philippians 3:10). Now use all the knowledge, love, life, and power you have already attained. So shall you continually go on from faith to faith (Romans 1:17). So shall you daily increase in holy love, until faith is swallowed up in sight and the law of love is established to all eternity.
